title: Breadcrumb trail with structured data
when: The user wants a breadcrumb that shows where a page sits in the site hierarchy and links back to parent pages.
inputs: the path from home to the current page
prompt:
Goal: A short linked trail announced as navigation and read by search engines as a BreadcrumbList.
Steps:
1. <nav aria-label="Breadcrumb"> with an <ol>; ancestors are links, the last item is the current page with aria-current="page".
2. Separators come from CSS (li + li::before { content: "/"; }) so they are not read aloud; a separator SVG is aria-hidden.
3. On narrow screens keep the first and the last two items and collapse the middle behind <button type="button" aria-expanded="false">.
4. Truncate a very long current title with text-overflow: ellipsis; the full text stays in the element.
5. Add BreadcrumbList JSON-LD whose itemListElement (position, name, item) matches the visible trail.
Quality bar:
- Names match the titles of the pages they lead to.
- The trail sits above the h1, small but at full contrast.
- Links show a focus outline.
Pitfalls:
- Separators typed as text and announced.
- Current page linked to itself without aria-current.
- JSON-LD names that differ from the visible trail.
Verify:
- [ ] A nav labeled Breadcrumb wraps an ol.
- [ ] The last item has aria-current="page".
- [ ] The JSON-LD parses and lists every level in order.
- [ ] The trail fits or collapses at 375 px.
Output: Breadcrumb markup above the page title, its CSS, and the JSON-LD in the head.

examples.input: breadcrumb for product pages: Home > Shoes > Running > Model X
examples.output: nav aria-label Breadcrumb, ol with three links and the current item, CSS chevrons, BreadcrumbList JSON-LD
